findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery credential is removed through local-storage API
findings.body: After RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() was changed to return federated credentials first, the allCodesUsed() branch still calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()). removeStoredCredentialById only removes a locally stored credential; for a credential owned by a user-storage provider (whose getCredentials() model may also have a null or provider-generated id not present in local storage) this is a no-op or fails, so the exhausted federated credential remains. The user is given the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action but the old exhausted credential stays in the federation, so configuredFor()/getCredential() keep seeing it and the login form can keep presenting it instead of a clean re-registration.

findings.title: Federating recovery codes drops userLabel and generated-at timestamp
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential builds the federated UserCredentialModel only from credentialModel.getType() and the JSON list of raw codes. The credentialModel passed by RecoveryAuthnCodesAction also carries the user-supplied label (generatedUserLabel) and the generation timestamp, which the local-storage fallback preserves via createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel), but the federated path discards both. A user-storage provider therefore cannot persist/display the label the user entered (it is shown for the credential in account/admin views) and must invent its own creation date, so federated and local recovery-code credentials behave inconsistently.

findings.title: Login bean assumes federated credential is a fully parsed RecoveryAuthnCodes model
findings.body: The bean calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) and immediately does credentialModelOpt.get(), createFromCredentialModel(...), and getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() with no empty/exhausted handling. getCredential() now returns whatever the federation returns from getFederatedCredentialsStream(), which for a provider that supports the type for validation/update may be a plain CredentialModel whose credentialData is not the hashed RecoveryAuthnCodes credential-data structure (the new update path in CredentialHelper sends only a raw JSON list of codes). In that case createFromCredentialModel produces a model with no codes and getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() throws NoSuchElementException, turning the recovery-code login page into a server error instead of rendering the code prompt.

findings.title: New getCredentials() NPEs for unknown user
findings.body: getCredentials() does var myUser = getMyUser(user); and immediately dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes / myUser.otp without the null check that isConfiguredFor() and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() perform. getMyUser() returns null for a username not present in the storage map, so any credential listing for such a user (e.g. via getFederatedCredentialsStream during login/account calls) throws NullPointerException instead of returning an empty credential stream.
